title: CSCI 141 — Computer Science I
subject: Algorithms and Theory
description: An independent, catalog-aligned learning companion. It is not an official RIT course section or a replacement for the instructor's syllabus.
outcomes: Define and apply the three core components of a disciplined solution: precise problem specification, correctness argument, and resource bounds.
Explain how loop invariants support proof by initialization, maintenance, and termination to verify algorithm correctness.
Demonstrate how divide-and-conquer algorithms split problems, solve subproblems, and combine results to achieve efficient solutions.
